source: DOE Oil Industry Management Bureau, Prior Notice on Price Adjustments (weekly PDF, URL derived from the week it covers)
transformations: derive the document slug from each Tuesday-to-Monday pricing week
extract text with pypdf; read the covering week from the heading and prefer it over the requested week
industry figure from the summary row where present, else the modal company figure; mode not mean so one company cannot drag it

the mode is taken over blocs of filings within 0.10 PHP/L of each other rather than over exactly equal values, and the reported figure is the mode WITHIN the winning bloc, so it is always a value some company posted

a week is published only if at least 2 companies filed a gasoline figure and the winning bloc holds a strict majority of them; corrected 2026-08-21, when the summary row was found to bypass this check entirely, and the 7 weeks it had published on filings that do not support them were withdrawn
units: PHP per litre, change for the week
notes: The announced move, not a forecast. Announced Monday, effective 6:00 AM Tuesday, and holds for the week. The `consensus` column is the share of companies inside the winning bloc, NOT the share posting an identical figure; the two differ wherever companies filed the same move to different centavos, and figures written before 2026-08-19 carry the stricter meaning. Corrected 2026-08-21: 7 of the 24 weeks carried a figure taken from the notice summary row while the filings beneath it showed no majority, one of them read from a single company. Those figures are withdrawn and the weeks now read no_consensus; `consensus` and `n_companies` are kept as the record of why. The underlying documents were not re-fetched, so `retrieved_at` is unchanged and this is a re-reading of data already on file.
